body:
- A combined Western checklist would ask:
  - Is it understandable (inside your circle of competence)?
  - Is ROCE/ROIC above 15–20% over a full cycle?
  - Is reinvestment runway long (Fisher #1, Mayer, Sleep)?
  - Is debt low?
  - Are management honest owner-operators?
  - Is the price at or below a conservative intrinsic value, judged by an owner-earnings or FCF yield?
  - Will you hold for years?
- Graham's rules work as a safety screen, for balance sheet and earnings stability. They are less useful for finding compounders: modern high-ROIC, asset-light firms rarely trade below 1.5x book.
- Munger's 6% vs 18% quote is the conceptual bridge from Graham (cheap) to Buffett/Smith (quality). Over long holding periods, the return on capital dominates the entry multiple.

`strategy:klarman-margin-of-safety` | confidence: **verified** | tags: global, process, value, avoid-ruin

Principles from Margin of Safety (1991) and Baupost letters: (1) Value conservatively (liquidation, private-market or cash-flow value) and buy only at a large discount - the discount is the protection against your own errors. (2) Think about downside first; absolute, not relative, returns. (3) Look where selling is non-economic: forced or constrained sellers (index deletions, spin-offs, bankruptcy, fund redemptions, regulatory rules) and complex/illiquid securities. (4) Catalysts (asset sales, buybacks, restructuring) shorten the wait. (5) Hold cash when nothing qualifies - cash is a call option on future bargains. Indian forced-seller situations: MF scheme recategorisation (2017-18), index exits, promoter pledge invocations, ASM/GSM-listed stocks after rule-driven selling, demerged entities on listing, rights-issue discounts. Evidence: Baupost's strong first 25 years and weak post-2014 decade show the method depends on the opportunity set - it shines after crashes and lags in long, liquidity-driven bulls.

Links: person:seth-klarman (about); insight:avoid-ruin (similar_to)

Sources: <https://ivey.uwo.ca/bengrahaminvesting/resources/interviews-notes/seth-a-klarman> ; <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-01-22/baupost-clients-pulled-7-billion-since-2021-after-poor-returns>

body:
`case_study:bajaj-finance-2009-2021` · tickers: BAJFINANCE · confidence: verified

Split/bonus-adjusted (2016 split+bonus, 2025 4:1 bonus + 1:2 split, ~100x factor) price ₹0.50 (Mar 2009) → ₹786 (Oct 2021) ≈1,570x; ₹1,093 on 19 Nov 2026 (ATH ₹1,141, Jul 2026). Twin engine: trailing P/E 9 → 121 (13x) × implied EPS ~117x. Max drawdown inside the run −61% (Feb–May 2020, COVID moratorium); before the run it had fallen −90% (2006–09). Early signal: Aug 2007 Rajeev Jain hired from AIG; the business was ~90% auto finance; 2008–10 it cut risky segments and pivoted to consumer durables, SME and later 34 products (by 2015); renamed 2010. In FY10–13 profits rose fast while the stock sat at P/E ~7–12 (2011 year-end 6.8). FY15–20: revenue +30–45%/yr with ROE 19–22%. Investors who caught it held through −32% (2013), −31% (2018) and −61% (2020). Ended/stalled: P/E peaked at 121 in Oct 2021; from Oct 2021 to Nov 2026 EPS rose ~4.8x but P/E fell to ~36, so the stock gained only ~39% in 5 years. Lesson: a lender multibagger needs underwriting proven through a credit cycle and a cheap starting multiple; at 100x+ even 5x EPS growth gives flat returns. NPA 2%→12% in 2009 claim is blog-sourced (unverified).

Key data: **start_year**: 2009; **end_year**: 2021; **start_price**: 0.5; **end_price**: 786; **price_nov2026**: 1093; **multiple**: ~1,570x (to 2021 peak); ~2,190x to Nov 2026; **pe_start**: 9.0; **pe_end**: 120.8; **pe_multiple**: 13x; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~117x; **max_drawdown**: -61% (2020); **early_signals**: 2007 CEO hire; pivot from auto to consumer durables/SME; profits compounding at P/E <12 in 2010-13; **ended**: P/E 121 in 2021, de-rated to ~36 while EPS grew; **lesson**: Starting multiple and credit-cycle survival matter more than growth narrative

Sources: <https://www.screener.in/company/BAJFINANCE/> · <https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/cover-story/story/indias-best-ceos-2015-rajeev-jain-bajaj-finance-into-fastest-growing-nbfcs-54964-2015-12-29> · <https://www.outlookbusiness.com/lead-story/creating-a-legacy-of-his-own-3716> · <https://ajuniorvc.com/?p=8480>

body:
**Formula.** Take cumulative CFO over N years and divide it by cumulative PAT over the same years. Use N = 5, because single years are noisy.

**Thresholds (practitioner convention; Marcellus-style screens use CFO/EBITDA of at least 70–80%).**

| Ratio | Reading |
|---|---|
| ≥ 0.9 | Healthy |
| 0.7–0.9 | Explain it |
| < 0.7 | Red flag (flag #1 in `insight:forensic-redflag-checklist`) |
| < 0 while PAT is positive for 3+ years | Presumptively disqualifying until explained |

**Worked example A: Gensol Engineering (GENSOL), consolidated, FY20–FY24**

| | FY20 | FY21 | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | Σ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PAT | 2 | 3 | 11 | 23 | 53 | **92** |
| CFO | −18 | 6 | −50 | 115 | −98 | **−45** |
| Capex (CFO − FCF) | 0 | 0 | 51 | 439 | 479 | 969 |
| FCF | −18 | 6 | −101 | −324 | −577 | **−1,014** |
| Borrowings (year-end) | 11 | 11 | 82 | 598 | 1,510 | |

- Cumulative CFO/PAT = −45 / 92 = **−0.49**.
- Reported profit grew 26x over the period, while the business consumed cash every year except one.
- The ₹1,014 cr of FCF burn was funded by borrowings, which rose ₹1,499 cr, and by equity.
- SEBI's interim order of 15-Apr-2025 later found that EV term loans had been diverted to promoter uses (see `insight:ind-as-accounting-levers`).
- **Visible at the time:** CFO was negative in 3 of 5 years while PAT compounded, and debtor days stood at 86 in FY24. The cash test alone would have kept you out.

**Worked example B: Asian Paints (ASIANPAINT), FY22–FY26. A quality company with one bad year.**

| | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 | Σ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PAT | 3,085 | 4,195 | 5,558 | 3,710 | 4,395 | 20,943 |
| CFO | 986 | 4,193 | 6,104 | 4,424 | 7,088 | 22,795 |

- FY22 CFO/PAT was **0.32**. Inventory was built during the raw-material inflation, and CCC went from 59 days to 94.
- The 5-year ratio is **1.09**.
- **Lesson:** one bad year in a business with a long clean history is a working-capital swing. Several bad years in a young, fast-growing business is a pattern. Always look at the cumulative figure.

body:
- Screener's "Borrowings" includes lease liabilities, so asset-light retailers look indebted.
- Goodwill from a PE buyout crushes reported ROE and ROCE. Use return on tangible equity.
- Ind AS 116 EBITDA overstates margins of rent-heavy models by 4–6 pp. Always find the pre-Ind AS number (company presentation, or EBITDA − lease cash outflow).
- Viral social-media "ground data" can be fake (the VMM guard-recruitment meme was disowned by the company).
- Payback and SSSG are company-defined. Read the definition before quoting them.
- (v1.1) **Cost-plus transfer pricing caps margins.** Exports sold to the parent at cost + x% do not gain from a weak rupee. The parent captures it.
- (v1.1) **High ROCE can be borrowed from the group's balance sheet.** If the constrained product is made by a sister company, the listed entity's capital looks small.
- (v1.1) **Cost allocations from the parent can step up without notice** (Cummins: support services ₹111 → ₹223 cr in a year, then a further Q2 "true-up"). Read the other-expenses note every year, and the call's "one-offs" answer every quarter.
- (v1.1) **Company "ranges" can hide the number.** "DC = 30–40% of power gen" is ±₹130 cr a quarter, wide enough to hide a slowdown in the rest of the business.
- (v1.1) **Tool note:** `tools/nse_fetch.py transcripts SYMBOL --download DIR` ignores `--from/--to` and downloads everything. List first, then fetch only the URLs you need.

body:
- Screener's "Borrowings" includes lease liabilities, so asset-light retailers look indebted.
- Goodwill from a PE buyout crushes reported ROE and ROCE. Use return on tangible equity.
- Ind AS 116 EBITDA overstates margins of rent-heavy models by 4–6 pp. Always find the pre-Ind AS number (company presentation, or EBITDA − lease cash outflow).
- Viral social-media "ground data" can be fake (the VMM guard-recruitment meme was disowned by the company).
- Payback and SSSG are company-defined. Read the definition before quoting them.
- (v1.1) **Cost-plus transfer pricing caps margins.** Exports sold to the parent at cost + x% do not gain from a weak rupee. The parent captures it.
- (v1.1) **High ROCE can be borrowed from the group's balance sheet.** If the constrained product is made by a sister company, the listed entity's capital looks small.
- (v1.1) **Cost allocations from the parent can step up without notice** (Cummins: support services ₹111 → ₹223 cr in a year, then a further Q2 "true-up"). Read the other-expenses note every year, and the call's "one-offs" answer every quarter.
- (v1.1) **Company "ranges" can hide the number.** "DC = 30–40% of power gen" is ±₹130 cr a quarter, wide enough to hide a slowdown in the rest of the business.
- (v1.2) **US GAAP gross margin is not comparable across retailers.** Some put occupancy, distribution and buying in COGS (FIVE); others put them in SG&A. Compare operating margin, or rebuild merchandise margin.
- (v1.2) **One-off credits inside COGS.** FIVE's Q2 FY26 GAAP gross margin of 48.5% included a $163.6M tariff refund. Trailing GAAP EPS screens are wrong for four quarters. Always read the Ex-99.1 reconciliation.
- (v1.2) **Ownership-filing false alarms.** Vanguard's 13G/A shows 0% after its Jan-2026 realignment. The 13F still shows the shares.
- (v1.2) **"Average sales per store" usually counts only stores open the full year.** Also compute total sales ÷ average store count.
- (v1.2) **FCF in a slowdown-of-openings year is flattered** (capex and working-capital timing). Normalise before using it.
- (v1.2) **Tool notes:** use `sec_fetch.py doc T ACC --file NAME --text` for exhibits; `holdings13f` value can misparse (use shares); confirm the insider "non-10b5-1" flag on the form.
- (v1.1) **Tool note:** `tools/nse_fetch.py transcripts SYMBOL --download DIR` ignores `--from/--to` and downloads everything. List first, then fetch only the URLs you need.

- [ ] **US filers (v1.2):** 10-K item/note reading list done with a year-over-year text diff; non-GAAP reconciliation table by quarter; SBC table (SBC % of sales/NI/FCF, FCF − SBC, overhang, buyback-to-hold-flat); Form 4 summary (P/S only, 10b5-1 checked); 13F/13G holder changes with remarks read; management-change table from 8-K 5.02; promise tracker split long-range vs near-term
- [ ] Edge question (3 lines) written first
- [ ] Source tag on every number; `[EST]` with the method on every estimate; a second source or route for every key number
- [ ] Unit P&L table (fully loaded and, if possible, four-wall)
- [ ] Physical cost-driver table with at least one external-input sensitivity (wage, tariff, commodity) in bps, with lines ranked by weight first
- [ ] RPT table by year with share of each cost line
- [ ] **Parent-take table** (MNC subs/group cos): royalty, fees, TP formulas, dividends, renewal dates, as % of sales and EBITDA (v1.1)
- [ ] **Price-vs-cost lag table** (manufacturers): materials ratio by quarter, price-action dates, inventory layer, leading commodity series (v1.1)
- [ ] Core PBT (ex other income) and customer-concentration line (v1.1)
- [ ] Ownership and supply table (who sold, at what price, to whom; what is left; incentives and strike prices)

- [ ] Override table and open-flag count

- [ ] **S2 checklist (v1.3):** every disqualifier-v2 rule pass/fail/unknown with a dated source, filled before L1
- [ ] **L8 (v1.3):** worksheet run (bank mode for lenders) + decision card + paper calls; extra inputs collected (two-source dated close, 10 FY-end P/Es or P/Bs, 3+ peers, 6-month ADV, pending dilution)
- [ ] **Lenders (v1.3):** NPA walk with write-offs; growth ex special funding windows; per-outlet table; Schedule-16 cost table incl. DICGC and the PSL-shortfall line; funding-concentration table (state, NRI, top-20, bulk, period-end vs average); bad-but-benign / good-but-misleading table
title: deep_dive_protocol › Deliverables checklist

body:
- **S1** net worth < 0 (equity capital + reserves), unless payout-driven (FCF > 0 and 3-year dividends ≥ |net worth|).
  S1raw reported alongside.
- **S2** interest cover EBIT / interest < 1.5x (EBIT = operating profit − depreciation + recurring other income;
  negative EBIT with interest fires; no interest and debt < 5% of assets ⇒ not fired, else unknown).
  **S2b** India variant < 2.5x.
- **S3** (US definition, **reported only**): short-term borrowings > cash equivalents + 0.5 × CFO.
- **S4** dividends paid > 0 and > FCF while borrowings rose.
- **S5-India** = ≥ 2 of S1, S2, S4 (the live India definition). Secondary: S5b-India (S2b instead of S2), S5-US
  (≥ 2 of S1–S4, includes S3).
- **S3-India (exploratory, labelled so):** short-term borrowings > cash equivalents + investments (balance-sheet
  "Investments", total) + 0.5 × CFO. Standalone investments include stakes in subsidiaries, so this over-credits
  holding companies — a first cut only.
- Reference: **S0** EBIT < 0.
- Unknown flags are excluded from that flag's statistics (coverage reported).

body:
- **Choose sites to test hypotheses.** Use a mature unit, a new unit in a new geography, and a different format or near-cannibalising unit. Visit off-peak and peak.
- **Count before you talk:** queues, bills per hour, footfall, staff and guards, facings, prices of a fixed basket. Numbers first, opinions second.
- **Talk to five constituencies:** staff, store or plant manager, customers, neighbours/competitors, and a supplier, landlord or driver. Ask about pay, tenure, rent, trips, and switching.
- **Ethics:** identify yourself honestly if asked. Never pay for or solicit confidential or unpublished price-sensitive information (that is insider-information risk). No recordings without consent.
- **Repeat the fixed price basket quarterly.** It is a cheap time series nobody else has.
- **B2B version (v1.1).** Use three visits: (A) an OEM or channel partner and two competitor dealers in the same city, (B) the company's dealer workshop or parts counter, (C) end-users and installers.
  - Count: price sheets *by product node* (same nodes every quarter), price-hike dates and percentages by component, lead times by platform, service bays and jobs, and a fixed basket of 5 spare parts (genuine vs will-fit).
  - Ask end-users the engineering ratio that sizes demand (e.g. DG MW per IT MW).
- **Output:** a "surprises vs model" list. Each model estimate is marked confirmed, contradicted or no read.
